Get Out The Vote! The midterm elections are on Tuesday. I’m a student. How do I vote? First, check to see if you’re registered to vote. If you’re from Idaho, go to idahovotes.gov to look up your registration status. Voter registration in Idaho is tied to your physical address. You might be registered to vote where you live with your parents. If you lived in Moscow and voted in the 2016 election, your old registration is probably still in the system—but if you’ve moved since then and have a new address, you need to re-register. If you are already registered, good job! (Nicole Skinner is probably proud of you.) If you aren’t registered yet, or want to re-register here in Moscow, the deadline to register online or through the mail has already passed. Lucky for you, Idaho lets you register on Election Day! On Tuesday, go to the Latah County Fairgrounds 1. Bring a photo ID with you. That can be an Idaho driver’s license or your Vandal Card. You can also use your passport, a tribal photo ID card, or a concealed weapons license. If you’re going to register in-person on Election Day, you’ll also need to bring a document with your current address. That can be something like a copy of your lease, a bank statement, or a utility bill. Sources: https://idahovotes.gov/citizens-guide/, https://idahovotes.gov/student-and-residency- voting/, https://www.acluidaho.org/en/know-your-rights/aclu-voter-your-rights-voter 1 In previous elections there were poling locations at the Kibbie Dome, but not this year. If you’re interested, you can read more about that on the Argonaut wbsite. Links in description.
